domain_rule: UNKNOWN negates to UNKNOWN; WIN and LOSS swap; DRAW is fixed.
Immediate terminal action is exact WIN or final-board DRAW.
A state resolves WIN if any action is known WIN.
If no action is WIN and at least one action remains UNKNOWN, the state remains UNKNOWN.
If all actions are exact and at least one is DRAW, the state is DRAW.
If all actions are LOSS, the state is LOSS.
theorem_candidate.induction: In a finite acyclic alternating game, synchronous iteration from UNKNOWN resolves a winning state at 1 + the minimum resolution time of a losing child, and a losing state at 1 + the maximum resolution time of winning children. This is exactly faster-win/slower-loss strong distance. Draws resolve when the finite continuation is exhausted without a forced win/loss.
theorem_candidate.consequence: Strong score is derivable as (resolved outcome, first resolution iteration); the finite strong-score chain need not be treated as a primitive value carrier.

relation_to_shell_tests.value_specific_bellman_orbit: exactly matches strong state/action semantics on all complete controls
relation_to_shell_tests.caution: This experiment establishes a value-specific refinement orbit / generated abstract domain. It is not yet a proof that this four-valued domain is the unique forward-complete shell in the full abstract-interpretation sense.

relation_to_boundaries: WIN-resolved-by-k sets were upward closed under the support-local favorable q order in every tested case.
LOSS-resolved-by-k sets were downward closed in every tested case.
Therefore the four-valued Bellman refinement can be represented symbolically by the same extremal antichain boundary machinery.
literature_alignment: Win/draw/loss/unknown retrograde databases propagate partial information by the same existential-win / universal-loss rules.
Generalized strong-preservation theory warns that raw-transition partition shells can be needlessly fine and allows non-partitioning abstract domains.
The observed RBA boundary domain is a non-partitioning monotone representation of the value-specific refinement.
